# What is the new ESPN DTC service? Plans, costs, key facts

ESPN

- ESPN

Aug 21, 2026, 12:30 AM

ESPN launched a direct-to-consumer service in August 2025. The service offers major enhancements within ESPN's streaming and app experiences. Here are key facts to know:

New streaming plan details

When did ESPN direct-to-consumer launch?

The service brought the full suite of ESPN networks and services directly to fans in August 2025.

How can I subscribe to ESPN direct-to-consumer?

Fans can sign up for the new service here.

What plans does ESPN direct-to-consumer offer?

Fans can choose from two plans:

ESPN Unlimited Plan

- Access to all of ESPN's linear networks -- ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network -- in addition to ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX
- 47,000 live events a year, on demand replays, studio shows, original programming and more

ESPN Select Plan

- Access to all content available on ESPN+
- More than 32,000 live sports events annually, a robust library of exclusive studio shows, on-demand replays, acclaimed original content and more

How much does each plan cost?

ESPN Unlimited Plan: $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year

ESPN Select Plan: $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year

What is available only on the ESPN Unlimited Plan vs. the ESPN Select Plan?

ESPN Unlimited Plan subscribers have access to all ESPN networks, including ESPN+, with events like NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, tennis and golf majors, top-tier college football and basketball, WWE and postseason coverage from all those and more.

ESPN Select Plan subscribers have access only to ESPN+, with top-tier soccer, PGA Tour, NHL, UFC and a selection of college sports, tennis, PLL, UFL and other leagues.

Customers with Hulu + Live TV, DIRECTV, Fubo TV, Spectrum TV, Verizon FiOS, U-verse, Cox, Comcast Xfinity, and other supported providers may already get ESPN Unlimited as part of their pay-TV package, with more partners to come. To activate your ESPN plan or to learn more, please visit the ESPN Fan Support Activation FAQ.

Do both plans include advertising?

Like linear television, both plans have ads during live events and studio shows. Bundle options with Disney+ and Hulu will be available with or without ads on those platforms.

New app plan details

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact the overall ESPN app experience?

The enhanced ESPN app integrates game stats, betting information, fantasy sports, commerce, multiview options and a personalized SportsCenter For You. The new features and functionality are available to all fans who watch sports on the ESPN App, whether they subscribe directly or through pay-TV.

If I already use the existing ESPN App, do I need to download anything else with ESPN direct-to-consumer?

All features are available within the existing ESPN App on mobile devices and connected TV.

Impact of ESPN direct-to-consumer on existing plans

If I am an ESPN+ subscriber, do I still have access to the same content?

ESPN+ will continue to be available in a variety of ways. Existing ESPN+ subscribers will become subscribers to the ESPN Select Plan.

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers?

Existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers will become subscribers to a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ Select bundle and continue to receive the same content through the ESPN and Disney+ apps.

Can subscribers still get ESPN via cable bundles with direct-to-consumer?

ESPN will continue to be distributed via pay-TV providers. Pay TV subscribers will have access to the enhanced features within the ESPN App via their pay-TV subscriptions.

Two landmark deals were announced in August 2025 that expanded ESPN's media footprint and further enhanced the entertainment experience for sports fans.

ESPN's streaming app now costs $13.99 a month for Select and $31.99 for Unlimited - The Money Overview

# ESPN’s streaming app now costs $13.99 a month for Select and $31.99 for Unlimited

 By Tyler Foster 

 Published September 28, 2026 

 Image Credit: AirportExpert - CC0/Wiki Commons 

A monthly ESPN Select subscription now costs $13.99, and ESPN Unlimited costs $31.99, according to ESPN’s own pricing page, up from $12.99 and $29.99. The stand-alone app, sold as a way to watch live sports without a cable package, rolled out this increase on a subscriber-by-subscriber timeline tied to when someone originally signed up, a different mechanic than the single companywide date Disney applied to Disney+ and Hulu the same month.

What a rising ESPN bill doesn’t cover: The Senior Property Tax & Home-Cost Relief Kit offers an application log and renewal calendar for the property-tax side of the same household budget. Log renewal dates for property-tax relief programs →

## Two tiers, one app, two different dollar jumps

ESPN Select rose from $12.99 to $13.99 a month, or from $129.99 to $139.99 a year, while ESPN Unlimited rose from $29.99 to $31.99 a month, or from $299.99 to $319.99 a year, according to ESPN’s own plans-and-pricing support page. In dollar terms, Unlimited’s two-dollar monthly increase is twice the one-dollar increase applied to Select, even though the two moves work out to roughly similar percentage jumps, about eight percent for Select and about seven percent for Unlimited.

On an annual basis the same ratio holds: Select’s yearly price rose from $129.99 to $139.99, a ten-dollar jump, while Unlimited’s yearly price rose from $299.99 to $319.99, a twenty-dollar jump, exactly double Select’s increase in both the monthly and annual figures. That consistency, Select always moving by half of what Unlimited moves, points to both tiers being priced off the same underlying formula rather than adjusted independently of each other.

Both figures match what Sports Media Watch reported when the change was first announced, and the outlet noted these are the first price increases ESPN has applied to Select and Unlimited since the direct-to-consumer app launched in 2025. A year without a price change, followed by one increase across both tiers at once, is a different rhythm than the smaller, more frequent increments Disney has used on the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu tiers.

ESPN Select and Unlimited are sold as stand-alone subscriptions, watched through the ESPN app rather than bundled into a cable package, positioning them as an alternative for a household that has already dropped traditional pay television. The new prices apply to that direct subscription regardless of whether a household also carries a Disney+ or Hulu subscription through some other arrangement.

## A grandfather date instead of a single rollout day

ESPN’s own support page describes a mechanic tied to two specific dates rather than a single companywide rollout: anyone who subscribed before August 20, 2026 keeps the old $12.99 or $29.99 price until their first billing date after September 17, 2026. That creates a window of nearly a month, from August 20 to September 17, during which the exact price a subscriber pays depends on precisely when they signed up.

That two-date structure differs from how Disney rolled out its own Disney+ and Hulu price changes the same month, where new subscribers paid the higher price immediately and existing subscribers moved up on their very next bill, with no multi-week grandfather period described in that coverage. ESPN’s approach effectively gave subscribers who joined just before August 20 close to a full extra month at the old rate before the new one took hold.

Because monthly billing dates are spread across every day of the month depending on when a subscriber first signed up, “first billing date after September 17” is not one single day for the entire subscriber base. Someone billed on the 18th of each month saw the new

ESPN Unlimited vs ESPN Select: Which Tier Wins in 2026?

# ESPN Unlimited vs ESPN Select: Which Tier Wins in 2026?

 Updated Aug 31, 2026 13 min read 

 The SmartTVs Lab · Editorial team · since 2023 

 Quick Answer 

ESPN's price list showed Select at $13.99/mo ($139.99/yr) and Unlimited at $31.99/mo ($319.99/yr) when read August 31, 2026. It says subscribers from before August 20 retain their price until the first billing date after September 17.

 In this guide 

ESPN Unlimited vs ESPN Select is the decision ESPN subscribers face after the ESPN+ brand split into a 2-tier direct-to-consumer structure. This guide maps each sport, shows the Disney Bundle math, and explains the current US UFC route through Paramount+. Compare DAZN separately if boxing is your priority.

- ESPN Select is listed at $13.99/mo or $139.99/yr, based on ESPN’s price page read August 31, 2026
- ESPN Unlimited is listed at $31.99/mo or $319.99/yr, with all linear ESPN channels on top of Select
- The $21.99/mo Disney Bundle pairs ESPN Select with Disney+ and Hulu at a discount to the three published standalone prices
- UFC no longer separates the ESPN tiers in the US because numbered events and Fight Nights moved to Paramount+ in 2026 with no event fee
- If you already have YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo, or cable with ESPN, neither tier adds value for live ESPN, you already have the app access through that login

## What Changed in August 2025: The ESPN+ Rebrand

ESPN retired the ESPN+ brand in August 2025 and replaced the direct-to-consumer lineup with two tiers instead of one. The lower tier kept the old ESPN+ content library and got renamed ESPN Select. A new premium tier, ESPN Unlimited, launched above it with live linear ESPN channels included.

ESPN’s own DTC explainer draws the line cleanly. It states that “ESPN Select Plan subscribers have access only to ESPN+,” while “ESPN Unlimited Plan subscribers have access to all ESPN networks, including ESPN+.” That single sentence is the entire decision in this comparison.

According to ESPN’s own Fan Support page as of 2026-04-20, the Select tier continues the same broad slate of live events that ESPN+ carried pre-rebrand, while Unlimited is an entirely new product that replaces the need for a cable or YouTube TV login to watch live ESPN in the app. The Verge’s August 2025 rebrand coverage confirms that Disney positioned Unlimited as direct competition to a $30-ish cable sports tier.

The rebrand wasn’t a price cut. ESPN’s published list showed Select at $13.99/mo when read August 31, 2026, above the old ESPN+ $11.99 price. The real change is that Unlimited exists as an option at all, which matters for cord-cutters who previously had no way to watch live ESPN primetime without paying for a full live-TV package.

To watch live ESPN primetime in the app, an Unlimited subscriber signs in with a MyDisney account, which unlocks the linear ESPN feed plus the on-demand library Select already carried.

## ESPN Unlimited vs ESPN Select: The 2-Way Comparison

ESPN Select Best Value

Choose this if you mostly watch on-demand and non-marquee live events.

- $13.99/mo or $139.99/yr as listed August 31, 2026
- MLB out-of-market, NHL, MLS, La Liga
- UFC moved to Paramount+ in the US in 2026
- College football and basketball (non-marquee)
- Full 30 for 30 documentary catalog

ESPN Unlimited Best Overall

Choose this if you want live ESPN, MNF, and CFP games.

- $31.99/mo or $319.99/yr as listed August 31, 2026
- Everything in Select, plus:
- Live ESPN / ESPN2 / ESPNU / SEC / ACC
- ABC simulcasts, Monday Night Football
- College Football Playoff and other ESPN exclusives

ESPN Select vs. ESPN Unlimited: Which Tier Do You Actually Need in 2026? · FULLTVBOX

 GUIDE ◆ NEW · By FullTVBox Test Bench · September 14, 2026 

# ESPN Select vs. ESPN Unlimited: Which Tier Do You Actually Need in 2026?

ESPN's two streaming tiers both got more expensive on September 17, 2026. Here's exactly what Select and Unlimited each include, the new prices, and which one is right for how you actually watch sports.

## The short version

- Both ESPN tiers got more expensive on September 17, 2026: Select is now $13.99/month ($139.99/year), Unlimited is now $31.99/month ($319.99/year) — a $1 and $2 monthly bump respectively.
- The tiers aren’t priced the same product at two speeds. Select is the ESPN+ streaming library only. Unlimited adds the actual live ESPN/ESPN2/ESPNU/SEC Network/ACC Network channel feeds, ESPN on ABC, and NFL Network.
- Most non-NFL sports fans only need Select. College sports, soccer, UFC, golf, and tennis are almost entirely an ESPN+ library, which Select already includes.
- Unlimited only pays for itself if you watch the live channels — Monday Night Football, SEC/ACC Network game windows, or NFL Network — none of which Select carries at any price.
- If you subscribed before August 20, 2026, you keep the old price until your next billing cycle after the increase lands.

ESPN quietly raised prices on both its streaming tiers effective September 17, 2026 — right as the fall sports calendar (college football conference play, the start of the NFL and NHL seasons) kicks into gear. If you’re deciding whether to sign up, downgrade, or just eat the increase, the two tiers aren’t actually the same service at two price points. Here’s what each one gets you.

## What changed on September 17, 2026

ESPN’s streaming lineup has two standalone tiers, both of which got more expensive this month:

| Plan | Old monthly | New monthly | Old annual | New annual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESPN Select | $12.99 | $13.99 | $129.99 | $139.99 |
| ESPN Unlimited | $29.99 | $31.99 | $299.99 | $319.99 |

It’s the first price change for Unlimited since it launched, and the second increase for Select (it started life as ESPN+ at $11.99). If you were already subscribed before August 20, 2026, you’re grandfathered in at the old price until your first billing date after September 17 — so the increase doesn’t hit everyone the same week.

The Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundles moved too, since ESPN’s tiers are one of the three ingredients: the ad-supported Select bundle went from $19.99 to $21.99/month, and the ad-free version from $29.99 to $32.99. If you’re weighing the bundle math on top of picking a tier, see our streaming bundles guide — the “worth it if you’d use all three apps anyway” logic still holds, just at slightly higher numbers.

## Select vs. Unlimited: what you actually get

The names suggest Unlimited is just “more of Select,” but the split is really streaming-only library vs. streaming-plus-live-channels:

ESPN Select is the ESPN+ content library: college football and basketball (a large slate, though not every nationally televised game), top-flight international soccer, the PGA Tour, NHL out-of-market games, UFC pay-per-view-adjacent content, tennis, and a long tail of niche sports ESPN+ has carried for years. It does not include the live ESPN or ESPN2 cable-style channel feed.

ESPN Unlimited includes everything in Select, plus the actual linear channels: ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network (and their “Extra”/”+” companion feeds), ESPN’s simulcast of ABC’s sports coverage, and NFL Network. That’s where Monday Night Football lives, along with the biggest nationally-televised college football windows and NFL Network’s own game slate — none of which Select carries, at any price.

The practical way to think about it: Select is “the ESPN app as a sports library,” Unlimited is “the ESPN app plus the cable channels you’d otherwise need a live-TV service for.”
